from.place: Proof input for the affine closed-immersion restriction: the auxiliary affine-site functor is continuous, fully faithful, and cocontinuous, and sends coverings to coverings.

title: Affine closed immersion site functor properties
statement: Let $i:Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\hookrightarrow X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be a closed immersion of affine schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-scheme]. Let $u:X_{\mathrm{app}}\to Z_{\mathrm{app}}$ send an affine ind-etale object $U\to X$ to $U\times_X Z$, and let $v:Z_{\mathrm{app}}\to X_{\mathrm{app}}$ be the functor of [def-exc-closed-site-lift]: for $V=\operatorname{Spec}\overline C$, set $v(V)=\operatorname{Spec}H_A(\overline C)$, where $H_A(\overline C)$ is the colimit of the etale finite-presentation factorizations $A\to B\to\overline C$ of [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift], with maps induced by postcomposition. These are functors on the affine ind-etale bases [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis] of the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Then $u$ is continuous [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $v$ is fully faithful and cocontinuous [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor], $v$ is left adjoint to $u$, and $v$ sends covering families to covering families. For every object $V$ of $Z_{\mathrm{app}}$, the geometric map induced by the quotient ring homomorphism $V\to v(V)$ is a closed immersion identifying $V$ with $v(V)\times_X Z$, and every point of $v(V)$ specializes to a point of $V$.

proof.text: First check that the specified constructions take values in the stated bases. For $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$ ind-etale over $A$, its closed base change is $\operatorname{Spec}(D/ID)$, ind-etale over $A/I$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. The indexing category defining $C=H_A(\overline C)$ is filtered by [lem-exc-closed-lift-filtered]; its terms are etale $A$-algebras of finite presentation by [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift]. Thus $C$ is ind-etale by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], and $v(V)=\operatorname{Spec}C$ lies in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. Postcomposition on the indexing categories induces the ring maps of [def-exc-closed-site-lift]; identity and composite postcompositions give identity and composite maps. Taking spectra reverses arrows, so this defines the asserted functor $v$. Base change is functorial by the uniqueness clause of [def-pc-fibre-product], defining $u$. All indexing categories are taken in the fixed universes/skeleton convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

proof.text: Let $V=\operatorname{Spec}\overline C$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$. By the contravariant affine correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the natural algebra bijection of [lem-exc-closed-lift-adjunction] reads $\operatorname{Hom}_X(v(V),U)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(V,u(U))$. This gives $v\dashv u$ with exactly the functors of step 1. By [lem-exc-closed-lift-reduction], the specified map $C/IC\to\overline C$ is an isomorphism, naturally in $\overline C$. Hence the adjunction unit $V\to uv(V)$ is an isomorphism. The map $V\to v(V)$ is the spectrum of $C\twoheadrightarrow C/IC\cong\overline C$, so it is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion] and identifies $V$ with the required closed base change. For $V,W$ the preceding Hom bijection with $U=v(W)$ becomes $\operatorname{Hom}_X(v(V),v(W))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(V,uv(W))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(V,W)$; the inverse is the map induced by $v$, by naturality and the unit identity. Thus $v$ is fully faithful.

proof.text: We will use the following elementary reading of the coverings in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. A covering family of affine objects has a finite jointly surjective subfamily: apply the fpqc condition to the whole affine target and enlarge the finitely many supplied affine source opens to their source objects. Conversely, a family of weakly etale maps between affines with a finite jointly surjective subfamily is fpqc. Indeed, every affine open $W$ of its target is covered by finitely many target principal opens $D(f_k)$ contained in $W$. To justify finiteness directly, a principal-open cover of any spectrum has elements generating the unit ideal: otherwise [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] supplies a maximal ideal missed by the cover. An expression $1=\sum_{k=1}^n a_k f_k$ gives a finite subcover. To apply this to the ambient principal opens contained in $W$, write $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Their intersections with $W$ are open in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and cover it; refine each by principal opens of $\operatorname{Spec}R$. The unit-ideal argument selects finitely many of these intrinsic principal opens, and hence finitely many of the original ambient principal opens covering $W$. The preimage of each target $D(f_k)$ in each selected affine source is the affine principal open obtained by inverting the image of $f_k$. These finitely many source opens have images covering $W$, as required. A maximal ideal is prime here by the elementary argument that if $ab\in\mathfrak m$ and $a\notin\mathfrak m$, an equation $1=c+ra$, $c\in\mathfrak m$, implies $b\in\mathfrak m$. This criterion includes empty targets and empty covering families.

source.place: Tag 09BK, lemma-closed-immersion-affines, definition of affine-site coverings, with Tag 098X lemma-affine-alternative and definition-standard-proetale; elementary fpqc interpretation

proof.text: The functor $u$ is continuous. A covering of $U$ is fpqc by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], so its base change along $U\times_X Z\to U$ is fpqc by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. The base-changed sources lie in the ind-etale basis and the arrows are weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. Thus it is a covering in the target basis [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. For $T\to U$ and a covering arrow $U_j\to U$, both $(T\times_U U_j)\times_X Z$ and $(T\times_X Z)\times_{U\times_X Z}(U_j\times_X Z)$ represent pairs of maps to $T,U_j$ agreeing in $U$, together with the compatible map to $Z$. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives mutually inverse canonical maps. These fibre products are affine and ind-etale by base change and composition stability, so they are fibre products in the full basis categories. This proves both clauses of continuity in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

proof.text: Every point of $\operatorname{Spec}C=v(V)$ specializes to a point of $V=\operatorname{Spec}(C/IC)$. Write the point as a prime $\mathfrak p\subset C$ and choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ containing it using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal]. For every $b\in IC$, the element $1-b$ maps to $1$ in $\overline C$ and is invertible by [lem-exc-closed-lift-units]. If $b\notin\mathfrak m$, maximality would give $1=c+rb$ with $c\in\mathfrak m$, so $c=1-rb$ would be a unit in the proper ideal $\mathfrak m$, a contradiction. Thus $IC\subseteq\mathfrak m$. The maximal ideal is prime by the calculation in step 3, and defines a point of $\operatorname{Spec}(C/IC)$ specializing from $\mathfrak p$: in the Zariski topology the closure of $\{\mathfrak p\}$ consists precisely of primes containing $\mathfrak p$. This is the requested specialization in the closed subscheme of step 2. If $C$ is the zero ring, there are no points and the assertion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 09BK, lemma-closed-immersion-affines, proof second paragraph: invertibility and specialization

proof.text: Let $\{V_a\to V\}$ be a covering. By step 3 choose a finite subfamily whose images cover $V$. The induced maps $v(V_a)\to v(V)$ are morphisms between ind-etale $X$-objects; on rings they are ind-etale, and therefore weakly etale, by the relative-map and weak-etaleness clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. They are flat by the weak-etale definition in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Their ring maps are flat, equivalently their affine scheme maps are flat, by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. Let $\mathfrak p$ be any point of $v(V)$ and choose a specialization $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m$ in $V$ from step 5. Choose $a$ and a point of $V_a$ over this point of $V$; the natural closed immersions of step 2 place it in $v(V_a)$ and its image is $\mathfrak m$, since the reduction identifications are natural. Apply [lem-sc-flat-going-down] to the flat ring map $C\to C_a$, the primes $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m$, and this prime of $C_a$ over $\mathfrak m$. It supplies a prime of $C_a$ over $\mathfrak p$. Thus the finite family $\{v(V_a)\to v(V)\}$ is jointly surjective. By step 3 it is a covering, and the entire image family is a covering as well. This proves that $v$ sends coverings to coverings; no finite-presentation or openness assertion for the flat maps is used.

source.place: Tag 09BK, lemma-closed-immersion-affines, proof third paragraph: images of coverings, flat going-down supplies generalizations

proof.text: To prove cocontinuity, take $V$ and a covering $\{U_j\to v(V)\}$ in $X_{\mathrm{app}}$. Step 4 gives a covering $\{u(U_j)\to uv(V)\cong V\}$ in $Z_{\mathrm{app}}$. Let $h_j:u(U_j)\to V$ be these arrows, using the inverse of the unit $\eta_V:V\xrightarrow{\sim}uv(V)$ from step 2. The counit gives maps $\epsilon_{U_j}:v(u(U_j))\to U_j$. They are maps over $v(V)$: naturality of $\epsilon$ and the triangle identity give $f_j\epsilon_{U_j}=\epsilon_{v(V)}v(u(f_j))=v(\eta_V^{-1}u(f_j))=v(h_j)$, where $f_j:U_j\to v(V)$. Thus the image of this covering under $v$ refines the original family, exactly as required by the cocontinuity definition [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor]. This argument requires only cocontinuity clause (1), not the stronger special-cocontinuity conditions.
